titulo.alumno: Comparing versions of a news story

intro: You will compare headlines and attributions, pointing out differences with evidence from the text.

texto: Compare which actor appears in the foreground, which verbs the headline uses and whether the source of a figure is attributed. A more intense verb can change the framing without changing the event. Don't infer bias from a single isolated word.

piezas.titulo: Two short items about a bus route

frases.estudio: A: «Ny bussrute gir kortere reisevei». Kommunen opplyser at rute 6 starter mandag, og at reisetiden reduseres med sju minutter for to holdeplasser. B: «Beboere får ny bussrute fra mandag». Bydelsavisa skriver at samme rute starter mandag. Den viser til kommunen for opplysningen om sju minutter.
frases.alumno: A: «New bus route shortens the journey». The council reports that route 6 starts on Monday and that travel time is cut by seven minutes for two stops. B: «Residents will have a new route from Monday». The district newspaper writes that the same route starts on Monday. It quotes the council for the seven-minute figure.

pregunta.texto: Which fact does the second version explicitly attribute to the council?

opciones.explicacion: The second version attributes this figure to the council.
The text doesn't mention any reaction from residents.
No information about the price is given.

pregunta.texto: Compare the angle of both headlines and explain which fact they share and how it is attributed.

textos: Overskrift A framhever kortere reisetid, mens B legger vekt på hvem som får den nye ruten. Begge sier at ruten starter mandag. Opplysningen om sju minutter knyttes til kommunen.

piezas.explicacion: Model: compare emphasis and keep attribution, without inferring an unproven intention.
